spec.purpose: Isolated two-matrix integer core: one FP16 estimate and one unsigned8 matrix product recover the low-byte congruence class under the explicit error128 condition. Both116-byte prepared row ranges retain original words, exception masks and trailing metadata. Compare2097152 dots per range against independent CPU integers and original four-IU8 hardware products, including all65536 original BF16 patterns. Report every recovery rejection and error-condition violation without declaring hardware proof. Only a numerically passing finite range enters16/64/256-group sequence comparison, with one warmup and three rotated attempts, all inputs and guards. Timings exclude preparation and canonical carry/exception costs. No model or product dispatcher changes.

implementation: One zero-C FP16 WMMA estimates each signed integer dot; one unsigned8 WMMA computes the exact residue modulo256 from the low bytes of signed cores. Exact recovery is conditional on native error strictly below128. Midpoints, nonfinite values and unsupported ranges reject. Headroom5/6 cap core magnitude at8160/16320; removed original BF16 bits remain in exception metadata. Both row layouts remain116 bytes. Original canonical carry and selective exception/remainder compensation are host-checked separately. GPU core timings compare original four-IU8 products on identical narrowed integer operands; the control uses the original116-byte stride and high/low offsets. They do not include canonical carry or exception work.
correctness_scope: All65536 original BF16 bit patterns, narrow/wide exponent spreads, extrema, mixed signs, cancellation, zeros and unsupported original rows are included. All2097152 generated integer dots per headroom compare with independent CPU sums and original four-IU8 hardware reconstruction. Every row word, raw source and guard is checked. Maximum observed native errors28/112 satisfy the conditional recovery premise in this finite sample; no universal hardware error bound is proved. Sequence outputs use those CPU-verified integer sums and are checked on all warmup and measured attempts. No real model is loaded, and no new GB10 operator/prompt or token result is claimed.
timing_scope: One warmup plus three rotating completed host measurements per variant for16/64/256 groups and1024 blocks. The16-group timings have pronounced sample-order variation and do not support a repeatable gain. At64 and256 groups both candidate ranges are slower. Initial preparation is separately measured once, includes both candidate and integer-control encoding, and is excluded from sequence clocks. Allocations, resets and checks are outside sequence clocks; guarded full-process wall is included in evidence.
decision: Keep the two-matrix core isolated and do not integrate or expand it into full captured attention on this evidence. All sampled integer recoveries pass, but64/256-group medians are0.2024/0.6863ms versus original0.1852/0.5925ms at headroom5, and0.2190/0.6213ms versus0.1947/0.4906ms at headroom6. Reducing matrix instruction count is still insufficient after recovery and operand transport, even before the additional canonical compensation from narrower cores. The16-group median difference is not retained because samples visibly alternate. Next investigate a different dominant runtime surface capable of a seconds-scale reduction, preserving the GB10 gate.
